value.title: Additive pipeline plumbing + medical team registration
value.description: Risk-first integration linchpin. Add `medical-sop` as a new additive PipelineEngineName member (src/orchestrator/workflow/engine.ts) and widen every Zod enum that mirrors it (team pipelineShape at src/config/schema.ts:366 + the PipelineSectionSchema engine enum) in lockstep. Extend BOTH exhaustive switches in src/orchestrator/workflow/selector.ts: selectPipelineEngineForTeam returns a new MedicalSopEngine for a `medical-sop` team; selectPipelineEngine (the config/programming path that reads config.pipeline.engine and can never legitimately be medical-sop) handles the member defensively (fall through to TsPipelineEngine) so the switch stays exhaustive without changing programming behavior. Create a new src/medical/ module with a MINIMAL MedicalSopEngine stub (implements PipelineEngine; run returns a trivial PipelineResult for now), the GuardrailSet type filling Team.guardrails, and buildMedicalTeam(config) + registry wiring so loadTeam(config, 'medical') resolves to a Team with pipelineShape 'medical-sop'. Byte-zero impact on ts|skill|workflow and the programming team is a HARD requirement. This sprint is plumbing + skeleton only — gates, store, numerics, ingestion, egress, and retrieval are later sprints.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).

A unit test parses a config/team declaring pipelineShape 'medical-sop' successfully and asserts the TS union and the Zod enum agree.

loadTeam(config, 'medical') returns a Team with id 'medical', pipelineShape === 'medical-sop', and a concrete GuardrailSet object in its guardrails slot (not undefined). A unit test asserts these fields.

Regression: loadTeam(config) with no id still returns the byte-identical programming team (providers deep-equal resolveRoleProviders(config), pipelineShape === resolveEngineName(config), memoryNamespace unchanged); a test asserts the programming team and existing engine selection are unchanged.
No @anthropic-ai/sdk or openai SDK import appears anywhere under src/medical (grep returns nothing); the module is ESM/NodeNext with .js import extensions and strict TS.

nonGoals: Do not implement the consent gate, audit log, or disclaimer — that is Sprint 2 (the MedicalSopEngine stub may have placeholder hooks but no enforcement).
Do not implement the red-flag detector / GuardrailSet.evaluate logic — that is Sprint 3 (define the GuardrailSet TYPE only this sprint).
Do not implement HealthDataStore or NumericsQueryLayer — that is Sprint 4.

value.title: Consent gate, append-only audit log, and disclaimer footer (Gate 1 + audit substrate)
value.description: Implement the compliance substrate and wire it as the FIRST gate of the medical SOP. ConsentGate is fail-closed: when no ConsentRecord is present, MedicalSopEngine.run returns a refuse verdict and makes ZERO downstream calls. AuditLog appends IDs/enums-only entries to .bober/medical/audit-<date>.jsonl with O_APPEND|O_CREAT and file mode 0600 — never prompt text or health values. DisclaimerComposer produces a versioned per-response footer. ConsentGate depends on AuditLog (records a 'consent' event). This sprint wires consent + audit + footer into the engine stub from Sprint 1; the red-flag gate (S3), numerics (S4), and retrieval (S6/S7) are later.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript strict-mode typecheck passes with zero errors (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass including new collocated tests for ConsentGate, AuditLog, and DisclaimerComposer; the full pre-existing suite stays green.

Fail-closed consent: with no ConsentRecord present, MedicalSopEngine.run returns a refuse verdict (MedicalAnswer with shortCircuit/refuse semantics) and makes ZERO downstream calls — verified with a spy/fake for numerics + LLMClient asserted never invoked.
ConsentGate.recordConsent persists a ConsentRecord and ConsentGate.current()/hasConsent() round-trip it (consentVersion, acceptedAtIso, rulesetVersion, disclaimerVersion).

AuditLog.append writes to .bober/medical/audit-<date>.jsonl with file mode 0600 and append-only (O_APPEND|O_CREAT) semantics; a test asserts the file mode and that a second append adds a line without truncating the first.

Audit entries contain IDs/enums ONLY (event, rulesetVersion?, patternsetVersion?, ruleId?, tIso) — a test feeds prompts/health values through the SOP and asserts NO prompt text and NO health value substring appears anywhere in the serialized audit file.

DisclaimerComposer.footer() returns a non-empty string carrying disclaimerVersion, and every MedicalAnswer the engine produces includes the footer; all timestamps (acceptedAtIso, audit tIso) are injected parameters, asserted by a deterministic test (no wall-clock read).

nonGoals: Do not implement red-flag detection — GuardrailSet.evaluate still returns allow this sprint (Sprint 3 adds the detector).
Do not implement HealthDataStore or numerics (Sprint 4).
Do not implement ingestion (Sprint 5).
Do not implement EgressGuard, the full SOP ordering, or medications (Sprint 6).
Do not implement literature retrieval (Sprint 7).
Do not read timestamps from the system clock anywhere — timestamps are parameters.
stopConditions: No-consent => refuse + 0 downstream calls; audit is 0600 append-only IDs/enums-only with no PHI leak; footer carries disclaimerVersion; timestamps are injected
value.definitionOfDone: src/medical/ gains ConsentGate (hasConsent/recordConsent/current; fail-closed), AuditLog (append to .bober/medical/audit-<date>.jsonl, O_APPEND|O_CREAT, 0600, IDs/enums only), and DisclaimerComposer (versioned footer). MedicalSopEngine.run runs the consent gate FIRST: absent consent => refuse with zero downstream calls + a 'refuse' (or 'consent') audit entry; present consent => proceeds to the (still allow-only) guardrail and attaches the disclaimer footer to the MedicalAnswer. Timestamps are injected parameters. Build, typecheck, and all tests pass; no PHI in the audit file.
assumptions: ConsentRecord + AuditEntry shapes are per the spec data model. The audit 'date' in the filename is derived from an injected timestamp parameter, not Date.now().
ConsentRecord persists as JSON under .bober/medical/ (e.g. consent.json) via node:fs/promises; AuditLog uses an O_APPEND|O_CREAT file handle with mode 0600.

MedicalAnswer.shortCircuit/abstained/refuse semantics: a consent refusal sets a refuse-style MedicalAnswer (body = canned consent-required message, abstained=false, shortCircuit semantics) — match the data model union.
ConsentGate depends on AuditLog (records a 'consent' event on recordConsent) per the architecture component graph.
value.generatorNotes:
Add small files under src/medical/: consent.ts (ConsentGate), audit.ts (AuditLog), disclaimer.ts (DisclaimerComposer), collocated *.test.ts. Wire them into the MedicalSopEngine stub from Sprint 1.

AuditLog: open with node:fs/promises fs.open(path, 'a', 0o600) or appendFile with mode; for the mode-0600 + O_APPEND guarantee prefer fs.open(path, constants.O_APPEND | constants.O_CREAT | constants.O_WRONLY, 0o600) then handle.write(JSON.stringify(entry)+'\n'). Ensure .bober/medical/ exists (fs.mkdir recursive, mode 0700). Filename audit-<date>.jsonl where <date> is YYYY-MM-DD derived from the injected tIso parameter — NEVER new Date()/Date.now(). The AuditEntry written must include ONLY: tIso, event, rulesetVersion?, patternsetVersion?, ruleId?. Do NOT serialize the prompt, the answer body, or any health value.

ConsentGate: hasConsent() reads .bober/medical/consent.json existence + validity; current() returns the parsed ConsentRecord | undefined; recordConsent(record) writes it (and appends a 'consent' audit entry via AuditLog). Fail-closed: hasConsent() false on missing/corrupt file.

DisclaimerComposer: footer() returns a fixed, non-empty, non-diagnostic wellness disclaimer string; expose readonly disclaimerVersion. Keep wording low-risk (general wellness, not diagnosis/treatment) consistent with the FFDCA posture in the architecture.

MedicalSopEngine.run ordering THIS sprint: (1) ConsentGate.hasConsent() — if false, append audit 'refuse' (ruleId 'consent-required'), return a refuse MedicalAnswer with the disclaimer footer, and DO NOT touch numerics/LLM; (2) else GuardrailSet.evaluate (still allow), then return a placeholder answer WITH the footer + an 'answer' audit entry. The timestamp used for audit/consent comes from opts or an injected clock param so tests are deterministic — thread a `now: string` (ISO) parameter or a small injected Clock; default it from opts.runId-independent injected value, not the wall clock.

Tests: assert no-consent => refuse + spy LLMClient never called + numerics fake never called; recordConsent round-trip; audit file mode === 0o600 (statSync mode & 0o777); append-only (two appends => two lines, first intact); PHI-leak test (feed a prompt containing 'my blood pressure is 180' and a health value, assert neither appears in the audit file bytes); footer non-empty + disclaimerVersion present; deterministic-timestamp test (inject a fixed ISO, assert it appears verbatim in the entry).

value.title: Red-flag emergency short-circuit (Gate 2, 0 LLM calls)
value.description: The headline safety guarantee. Implement a deterministic, pure/synchronous RedFlagDetector (categories cardiac|stroke|anaphylaxis|self-harm|overdose|none with a patternsetVersion) and the real GuardrailSet.evaluate (allow|short-circuit|refuse with rulesetVersion) wrapping it, wired into MedicalSopEngine.run immediately AFTER the consent gate and BEFORE any numerics or LLM call. A red-flag match returns a short-circuit verdict with a canned 911/988 escalation and makes ZERO downstream calls (no numerics, no retrieval, no LLM). The short-circuit is audited with ruleId + versions. This replaces the allow-only GuardrailSet stub from Sprints 1-2.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript strict-mode typecheck passes with zero errors (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass including new RedFlagDetector + GuardrailSet tests; the full pre-existing suite stays green.

For at least one representative prompt in EACH red-flag category (cardiac, stroke, anaphylaxis, self-harm, overdose), GuardrailSet.evaluate returns a short-circuit verdict with a canned escalation, and MedicalSopEngine.run makes ZERO LLM calls and ZERO numerics calls — verified with spy/fake dependencies asserted never invoked.
RedFlagDetector.detect is pure and synchronous (no async, no I/O, no network, no model): identical input yields identical RedFlagMatch across repeated calls, asserted by a test.
A non-emergency prompt returns category 'none' and the SOP proceeds past the guardrail to normal (allow) handling.
A short-circuit appends an audit entry with event 'short-circuit' carrying ruleId, rulesetVersion, and patternsetVersion (IDs/enums only — no prompt text).
GuardrailSet.evaluate throws on an empty prompt; the detector and guardrail require no network and no LLMClient (a test confirms no provider is constructed).

nonGoals: Do not implement HealthDataStore or numerics (Sprint 4) — the numerics dependency in run may remain a fake/stub this sprint.
Do not implement ingestion (Sprint 5).
Do not implement EgressGuard, medications, or the full retrieval SOP (Sprint 6).
Do not implement literature retrieval (Sprint 7).
Do not use an LLM for red-flag classification — detection is deterministic and local ONLY.
stopConditions: Every red-flag category short-circuits with a canned escalation and 0 LLM/numerics calls; 'none' proceeds; short-circuit is audited; evaluate throws on empty prompt
value.definitionOfDone: src/medical/ gains RedFlagDetector (pure detect(prompt): RedFlagMatch over a versioned pattern set, categories cardiac|stroke|anaphylaxis|self-harm|overdose|none) and a real GuardrailSet implementation whose evaluate(prompt, ctx) runs the detector first and returns short-circuit{rule,cannedResponse} on a match, refuse{rule,reason} for code-enforced refusals, else allow. MedicalSopEngine.run runs consent (S2) then GuardrailSet.evaluate; a short-circuit returns the canned escalation MedicalAnswer (shortCircuit=true) with the disclaimer footer + a 'short-circuit' audit entry and reaches NO numerics/LLM. Build, typecheck, and all tests pass.
assumptions: RedFlagMatch = { category: 'cardiac'|'stroke'|'anaphylaxis'|'self-harm'|'overdose'|'none'; ruleId?: string }. patternsetVersion is a string constant exported by the detector.

The pattern set is conservative keyword/phrase matching (case-insensitive, word-boundary aware) — deliberately favoring escalation reliability over paraphrase coverage (architecture ADR-2 accepts possible misses on novel phrasing).
self-harm/overdose escalate to 988 (US Suicide & Crisis Lifeline); cardiac/stroke/anaphylaxis escalate to 911. Canned responses are fixed strings, not model-generated.
The numerics dependency may be a fake this sprint; the LLMClient is injected so a spy can assert zero calls.
value.generatorNotes:
Add src/medical/red-flag.ts (RedFlagDetector + patternsetVersion) and src/medical/guardrails.ts (the real GuardrailSet replacing the S1 allow-only stub), collocated *.test.ts.

RedFlagDetector.detect MUST be a pure sync function: normalize the prompt (lowercase, trim), test against a per-category list of conservative patterns (word-boundary regexes or phrase includes), return the first matching category + a ruleId, else { category:'none' }. NO async, NO fs, NO network, NO LLM import. Export a patternsetVersion string (e.g. 'redflag-2026.06.16'). Keep categories: cardiac (e.g. 'chest pain' + radiating/short of breath), stroke (FAST: face droop, arm weakness, slurred speech, 'sudden numbness'), anaphylaxis ('throat closing', 'trouble breathing' + 'allergic'/sting/peanut), self-harm ('kill myself','suicidal','end my life'), overdose ('overdose','took too many','too much'). Favor reliability; document that novel phrasing may miss (ADR-2 risk).

GuardrailSet.evaluate(prompt, ctx): throw on empty/whitespace prompt; run detector; if category !== 'none' return { kind:'short-circuit', rule: ruleId, cannedResponse: escalationFor(category) }; (refuse branch for non-emergency code-enforced refusals can be a documented placeholder this sprint or minimal); else { kind:'allow' }. Expose rulesetVersion (e.g. 'guardrail-2026.06.16').

escalationFor(category): fixed strings. 911 for cardiac/stroke/anaphylaxis ('This may be a medical emergency. Call 911 (or your local emergency number) now.'), 988 for self-harm/overdose ('If you are in crisis, call or text 988 (US Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) now, or 911 if you are in immediate danger.'). NEVER model-generated.

MedicalSopEngine.run wiring: after consent gate, call this.guardrails.evaluate(prompt, ctx). On short-circuit: append audit { event:'short-circuit', ruleId, rulesetVersion, patternsetVersion } and return MedicalAnswer { body: cannedResponse, abstained:false, shortCircuit:true, citations:[], disclaimerFooter: footer() } WITHOUT calling numerics or the LLM. On allow: proceed to the placeholder normal path (numerics fake + footer). Inject the LLMClient and numerics layer so tests can spy.

Tests: parametrized over the 5 categories asserting short-circuit + spy LLM/numerics zero calls + audit entry; determinism (call detect twice, deep-equal); 'none' proceeds; empty prompt throws; assert guardrails.ts has no provider/network import.
value.evaluatorNotes:
sc-3-4: for each category, feed a representative emergency prompt to MedicalSopEngine.run with a spy LLMClient and a spy numerics layer; assert result.shortCircuit===true, body contains the right hotline (911 vs 988), and BOTH spies have zero calls.
sc-3-5: call detect(samePrompt) twice; deepEqual the results; assert the function is synchronous (not returning a Promise) and red-flag.ts imports nothing from src/providers or any network module.
sc-3-6: a benign prompt ('what was my average resting heart rate last week') => detect 'none' and run proceeds to the allow path.
sc-3-7: after a short-circuit, read the audit file; assert an entry with event 'short-circuit', a ruleId, rulesetVersion, patternsetVersion, and NO prompt text.
sc-3-8: evaluate('') and evaluate('   ') throw.
Full suite + build + typecheck green; confirm S1/S2 still pass (consent gate still fires before the guardrail).

value.title: HealthDataStore + deterministic NumericsQueryLayer
value.description: Implement the data + numerics layer that keeps arithmetic out of the LLM. HealthDataStore is a single generic events table (better-sqlite3 sync, mirroring FactStore) with INSERT OR IGNORE on a deterministic SHA-256 id of (metric|tStart|source|value); it exposes upsertObservations (returns NEW-row count), getObservations, getLabSeries, getBaseline/putBaseline, getPreference, close. NumericsQueryLayer exposes ONLY the closed NumericPrimitive whitelist (mean|min|max|latest|delta|slope|percentile|zscore) via getMetric plus getLabTrend; sampleCount 0 => value null (abstain). No eval, no codegen, no subprocess. The LLM never performs arithmetic.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript strict-mode typecheck passes with zero errors (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass including new HealthDataStore + NumericsQueryLayer tests (using temp dirs, no fs mocks); the full pre-existing suite stays green.

HealthDataStore.upsertObservations dedupes via INSERT OR IGNORE on the deterministic SHA-256 id and returns the count of NEW rows only: a test inserts N rows then re-inserts the same N and asserts the second call returns 0 while getObservations still returns N.
Each of the 8 NumericPrimitives (mean,min,max,latest,delta,slope,percentile,zscore) returns the correct value on a known fixture series (asserted against hand-computed expected values).
getMetric over an empty window returns NumericResult { value: null, sampleCount: 0 } (abstain) and does NOT throw; getLabTrend on an unknown biomarker abstains similarly.

NumericsQueryLayer reads the per-row unit and refuses (does not silently mix) aggregation across heterogeneous units for the same metric — a test with mixed units asserts a refusal/abstain rather than a blended number.
No eval, no Function constructor, no code generation, and no child_process/execa appears anywhere in the numerics code (grep/test over src/medical numerics files returns nothing).

nonGoals: Do not implement ingestion / SAX parsing (Sprint 5) — tests insert observations directly via upsertObservations.
Do not implement EgressGuard, medications, or the full SOP wiring (Sprint 6).
Do not implement literature retrieval (Sprint 7).
Do not add numeric primitives beyond the 8 whitelisted ones.
Do not store medications in HealthDataStore (medications are FactStore value-of-record — Sprint 6 / ADR-7).
stopConditions: Dedup + NEW-row count correct; all 8 primitives correct; empty window abstains; cross-unit refused; no eval/codegen/subprocess
value.definitionOfDone: src/medical/ gains HealthDataStore (better-sqlite3 sync, generic single events table + a lab_results table or shared table, deterministic SHA-256 id, INSERT OR IGNORE, the full accessor surface) and NumericsQueryLayer (closed NumericPrimitive whitelist + getLabTrend, sampleCount-0 abstain, cross-unit refusal). No eval/codegen/subprocess. Build, typecheck, and all tests pass.
assumptions: HealthObservation + LabResult + NumericResult shapes per the spec data model. The deterministic id is SHA-256 of `${metric}|${tStart}|${source}|${value}` (mirroring FactStore factId at src/state/facts.ts:58-69).
better-sqlite3 is already a dependency (used by FactStore at src/state/facts.ts); HealthDataStore uses the same sync API and a per-store db file path passed in (temp dir in tests).

slope is a simple linear least-squares slope over (t,value); percentile uses a documented method (e.g. nearest-rank or linear interpolation — pick one and test it); zscore is (latest - mean)/stddev. Document the chosen method in code.
Timestamps (tStart) are ISO string parameters on the observations; the store never reads the clock.
value.generatorNotes:
Add src/medical/health-store.ts (HealthDataStore) and src/medical/numerics.ts (NumericsQueryLayer), collocated *.test.ts.

HealthDataStore: model on FactStore (src/state/facts.ts) — same better-sqlite3 sync pattern. Single generic observations table: columns (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, metric TEXT, value REAL, unit TEXT, t_start TEXT, t_end TEXT, source TEXT). A separate lab_results table (id, biomarker, value, unit, collected_at, ref_low, ref_high) OR a typed view — keep labs distinct from observations. id = sha256(`${metric}|${tStart}|${source}|${value}`) via node:crypto (see facts.ts:58-69 for the exact factId helper to mirror). upsertObservations uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` in a transaction and returns db.changes summed (count of NEW rows). getObservations(metric, fromIso, toIso) filters by metric and t_start range, ordered by t_start. getBaseline/putBaseline + getPreference back a small key/value table. close() closes the db. All sync. Use node:fs/promises only for mkdir of the parent dir if needed.

NumericsQueryLayer(store): getMetric(window: MetricWindow, primitive: NumericPrimitive): NumericResult. Pull rows via store.getObservations(window.metric, window.fromIso, window.toIso). If rows.length === 0 => { primitive, value: null, unit: window.unit ?? '', sampleCount: 0 }. UNIT CHECK: collect distinct units across rows; if >1 distinct unit => abstain ({ value:null, sampleCount:0 }) or throw a documented 'cross-unit' refusal — pick abstain to match the no-throw contract, but make it observable (e.g. a separate reason) and TEST it. value.title: Apple Health ingestion (SAX streaming) + `bober medical import`
value.description: Implement bounded, streaming ingestion. IngestionNormalizer holds an IngestionAdapter registry and drives importFile through the matching adapter into the HealthDataStore via an ObservationSink. AppleHealthAdapter stream-parses Apple Health export XML via SAX with bounded (~1000-row) batches and pause/resume backpressure, never loading the whole ~4GB document into memory. A `bober medical import <file>` CLI command wires it end-to-end. importFile throws a clear error when no adapter canHandle the file.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript strict-mode typecheck passes with zero errors (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass including new ingestion tests against a fixture Apple Health XML; the full pre-existing suite stays green.

AppleHealthAdapter ingests a fixture Apple Health export XML via STREAMING SAX (no whole-file read): a test asserts the parser is fed via a read stream and that batches are flushed at a bounded cap (e.g. <=1000 rows per writeBatch).

Backpressure: the ObservationSink.writeBatch is awaited and the parse stream pauses/resumes around it so unbounded rows do not buffer in memory — asserted by a test using a slow sink that the parser waits on.
Re-importing the same file is idempotent: the second import adds 0 new rows (dedup via HealthDataStore INSERT OR IGNORE), asserted against the store row count.
IngestionNormalizer.importFile throws a clear error naming the problem when no registered adapter canHandle the file; register() adds adapters that canHandle dispatches to.
`bober medical import <file>` is registered in the CLI, callable, and reports an IngestionResult (e.g. new-row / total counts) on completion; a test or smoke invocation exercises the command wiring.

nonGoals: Do not add Whoop or CSV adapters — Apple Health XML only (the registry makes them additive later).
Do not implement EgressGuard, medications, or the full SOP wiring (Sprint 6).
Do not implement literature retrieval (Sprint 7).
Do not parse medications from the file into HealthDataStore (medications are FactStore value-of-record — Sprint 6 / ADR-7).
Do not load the whole document into memory at any point.
stopConditions: Apple Health XML streams via SAX with bounded batches + backpressure, re-import is idempotent, unknown files throw, and `bober medical import` works end-to-end
value.definitionOfDone: src/medical/ gains IngestionNormalizer (register/importFile + adapter registry), an ObservationSink that batches into HealthDataStore.upsertObservations, and AppleHealthAdapter (SAX streaming, bounded batches, backpressure). A `bober medical import <file>` CLI command (registered like src/cli/commands/run.ts) drives importFile and prints the IngestionResult. Build, typecheck, and all tests pass.
assumptions: A streaming SAX XML parser is available (e.g. an existing dep; if none, add a small well-known SAX dep such as 'sax' — justify in the PR and keep it light). Apple Health exports use <Record type="..." unit="..." value="..." startDate="..." endDate="..." sourceName="..."/> elements.
Record.type maps to HealthObservation.metric, value->value (parseFloat), unit->unit, startDate->tStart, endDate->tEnd, sourceName->source 'apple-health'. Non-numeric records are skipped.
writeBatch is async and awaited; the SAX stream is paused while a batch is flushing and resumed after (backpressure). Batch cap ~1000.
IngestionResult reports counts (recordsParsed, newRows) and is returned by importFile.

Add src/medical/ingestion.ts (IngestionNormalizer + ObservationSink + IngestionAdapter interface), src/medical/adapters/apple-health.ts (AppleHealthAdapter), and a CLI command src/cli/commands/medical.ts (or extend an existing command registrar) for `bober medical import <file>`. Collocate tests.

IngestionNormalizer: register(adapter) pushes to an array; importFile(filePath) finds the first adapter where canHandle(filePath) is true (e.g. by extension/sniff), else throw new Error(`No ingestion adapter can handle '${filePath}'`). Then await adapter.ingest(filePath, sink) and return its IngestionResult.

ObservationSink.writeBatch(obs, labs): await store.upsertObservations(obs) (sync call wrapped) + lab upsert; accumulate counts. Keep the sink small.

AppleHealthAdapter.ingest: open a read stream (fs.createReadStream) and pipe into a SAX parser (streaming, event-based). On each <Record> open tag, map attributes to a HealthObservation, push into a buffer. When buffer.length >= 1000: parser.pause() (or stream.pause()), await sink.writeBatch(batch, []), clear buffer, parser.resume(). On stream end, flush the remainder. NEVER fs.readFile the whole file. canHandle: filePath endsWith '.xml' and (optionally) a quick header sniff for 'HealthData' / 'export.xml'.

CLI: mirror src/cli/commands/run.ts registration. `bober medical import <file>`: build the medical HealthDataStore path under .bober/medical/health.db, construct the store + normalizer + AppleHealthAdapter, call importFile, print the IngestionResult counts, close the store.

FIXTURE: create a small test fixture Apple Health XML (a handful of <Record> elements) under a test dir; a test asserts streaming (spy that fs.readFile is NOT called for the whole file; or assert createReadStream is used), bounded batches (cap), backpressure (a sink that delays and a test that the parser awaited it), idempotent re-import (run twice, second newRows===0), unknown-file throw, and the CLI command exists + runs on the fixture.

If adding the 'sax' dep, keep it isolated to the adapter file and ensure it has no network surface (it does not).

value.title: EgressGuard + medications-in-FactStore + full SOP wiring (zero-egress end-to-end)
value.description: Wire the complete SOP under a code-enforced zero-egress default. EgressGuard exposes two independently opt-in axes (cloud-inference, literature-retrieval, both default false; assertAllowed throws when off). A `no-restricted-imports` ESLint block scoped to src/medical/**/*.ts forbids network modules everywhere except the one designated retrieval network file (created/stubbed here, real source in S7). Medications are read from FactStore.getActiveFacts (bi-temporal, ADR-7), never HealthDataStore. MedicalSopEngine.run is wired in full order: consent -> red-flag -> numerics -> meds -> egress check -> (literature disabled => abstain) -> disclaimer footer -> audit -> PipelineResult. With both axes off, a numeric question is answered from deterministic compute and a literature question abstains — default outbound bytes = 0.

value.title: MedlinePlus grounded retrieval + cited synthesis (opt-in)
value.description: The opt-in networked slice. Implement the real MedlinePlus / NIH (no-auth) source inside the single sanctioned retrieval network file (the ESLint exception from Sprint 6), reachable only after the literature-retrieval egress axis is opted in. retrieve returns disabled | abstain{reason} | grounded{passages}. synthesize runs the single LLM call (local Ollama default via the provider-agnostic LLMClient) and abstains unless a retrieved passage supports the claim; every non-abstained clinical claim carries >=1 citation. A source failure abstains — never fail-open. The cloud-inference axis stays independently off.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript strict-mode typecheck passes with zero errors (npm run typecheck).
Lint passes — the only network import in src/medical remains in the designated retrieval file (the ESLint boundary from Sprint 6 still holds).
All tests pass including retrieval + synthesis tests driven by RECORDED/FIXTURE MedlinePlus responses (no live network in CI); the full pre-existing suite stays green.

With literature-retrieval ON, LiteratureRetriever.retrieve queries MedlinePlus and returns grounded{passages} parsed from a recorded fixture response; with the axis OFF it still returns {disabled} (Sprint 6 behavior preserved).

synthesize abstains (abstained=true) when no retrieved passage supports the claim, and produces a cited answer (>=1 citation) when a passage does — verified with a fake LLMClient and fixture passages.

Fail-closed on source error: when the MedlinePlus source is unreachable/errors, retrieve returns abstain{reason} and synthesize emits an abstained MedicalAnswer — NO uncited clinical claim is ever produced (no fail-open path).

Axis independence: enabling literature-retrieval does NOT enable cloud-inference; synthesize uses the local Ollama model by default and there is no automatic cloud fallback (a test asserts the cloud-inference axis stays off and no cloud provider is constructed by the literature path).

nonGoals: Do not add PubMed/PMC or any second literature source — MedlinePlus/NIH only.
Do not build a cloud-inference synthesis path or any auto cloud fallback.
Do not call live network in tests — use recorded/fixture responses.
Do not relax the src/medical ESLint network boundary beyond the single sanctioned file.

Flesh out src/medical/retrieval/medline-source.ts (the sanctioned network file) and src/medical/retrieval/literature.ts (orchestration + synthesize). Collocate tests with committed fixtures.
